result.summary:
Ran docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md item by item against the actual diff at commit ba13b04 (branch feature/WF02-REQ-032, master...HEAD). Read in full: apps/bot/src/handlers/noShow.ts, apps/bot/src/scheduler/noShowJobs.ts, the domain/registration.ts additions (isNoShow, NoShowReasonCode/NO_SHOW_REASON_CODES/isNoShowReasonCode, getRegistrationNoShowContext, writeNoShowReason), the domain/notification.ts NotificationKind addition, the i18n/{types,en,ru}.ts additions, and the index.ts wiring diff. Read docs/agents/design/REQ-032.md and REQ-032-schema.md in full, plus REQ-031's step-02c security review as the precedent for this same S3-ownership-check pattern applied to a force_reply flow. Did not trust BACKEND-DEV's or REVIEWER's characterizations -- re-derived each finding from the code and constructed the negative case for each applicable invariant.

S3 (a member reads/acts only on their own registration) -- PASS, re-verified hard as directed, independently from REQ-031's precedent rather than assumed to transfer. Traced all three write-adjacent entry points in handlers/noShow.ts:
  - makeNoShowReasonCallbackHandler (lines 58-114): identity is resolved exclusively from the ACTING Telegram user via `tgId = ctx.from?.id` -> `flowUser = getFlowUserByTgId(db, BigInt(tgId))` (line 78-87) -- this never reads the registrationId encoded in callback_data as an identity claim, only as a row lookup key. `context = getRegistrationNoShowContext(db, registrationId)` (line 89) then resolves the row's ACTUAL owner from the DB. The ownership check at line 99, `if (context.userId !== flowUser.id)`, sits strictly BEFORE `ctx.answerCallbackQuery()` (the UX ack, line 104) and strictly before the write gate (line 108) and the call to writeNoShowReason (line 109). Constructed the negative case directly: a leaked or forwarded `noshow:reason:<code>:<registrationId>` callback_data string (e.g. registration belongs to user A, forwarded to or otherwise obtained by user B, tapped by B) resolves flowUser to B's own row via B's own tg_id, context.userId resolves to A's id from the registration table itself, the inequality fires, the function returns immediately after sending B the `notYours` alert -- no call to writeNoShowReason occurs on this path, confirmed by reading that the only call site of writeNoShowReason in this handler is textually after (and inside a branch reachable only past) the ownership check. B's own no-show state is also never touched, since the write always targets the registrationId embedded in the forged reference, i.e. A's row -- there is no path by which B's tap corrupts B's own unrelated registration either.
  - makeNoShowOtherCallbackHandler (lines 119-164): identical shape, identical ownership check at line 146, identical placement strictly before the free-text prompt is ever sent (line 155's already-answered short-circuit and line 160's prompt both sit after the check returns).
  - makeNoShowTextReplyHandler (lines 174-221): identity is resolved from `ctx.from?.id` (line 191), never from the replied-to message's contents. The registrationId is parsed from the REPLIED-TO message's own ref line via parseNoShowReplyContext (line 186), i.e. from a message the bot itself previously sent -- an attacker cannot manufacture a ref line pointing at someone else's registrationId that the target user would ever be replying to, since the ref line only ever appears in a force_reply prompt the bot sent to the actual registrant. Even so, the ownership check at line 201, `context === null || context.userId !== flowUser.id`, gates the write independently of that trust assumption -- confirmed by reading that writeNoShowReason (line 216) is reached only past this check. This is a silent no-op (not an alert) on ownership mismatch, correct for a passive listener per the same convention REQ-031's identical text-reply handler already established, and matching this design's own §4.3 step 6 spec verbatim.
In all three handlers, the check compares a DB-resolved owner (`context.userId`, read fresh via getRegistrationNoShowContext at request time, not cached/trusted from any prior state) against a DB-resolved acting identity (`flowUser.id`, read fresh via getFlowUserByTgId keyed on the acting Telegram user's own numeric tg_id) -- the registrationId itself, wherever it is sourced from (callback_data or a ref line), is used only as a lookup key, never as an authorization credential. This is exactly the pattern security-invariants.md S3 requires and the one REQ-031's step-02c review verified for its own analogous flow; re-derived independently here rather than assumed to transfer. PASS.

S2 (authorization is checked on the action) -- PASS, same evidence as S3 above; no role/EventStaff dimension applies to this flow (a registrant answering their own no-show question is not an organizer/staff action), so S2 collapses to the S3 ownership check already traced.

S9 (idempotency per (registration, kind), no in-memory state) -- PASS. makeNoShowReasonRequestJob (scheduler/noShowJobs.ts lines 133-157) routes its single send through the existing sendLedgeredNotification (domain/notification.ts, REQ-025, reused unchanged) with kind: 'no_show_reason_request' -- confirmed as the only new NotificationKind member (domain/notification.ts line 26, a one-line union addition, notification_ledger.kind already text, no migration). Idempotency is enforced by notification_ledger's UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) DB constraint (pre-existing, unchanged by this diff), not by any in-memory set or in-process cache -- grepped scheduler/noShowJobs.ts and handlers/noShow.ts for any module-level Set/Map/cache: none exists. Constructed the negative case: the job is re-run at T+24h and T+48h (AC3) against the same still-not-checked-in registration -- selectRegistrationsForNoShowReasonRequest (lines 44-69) re-selects the same candidate each time (its WHERE clause has no NOT EXISTS-against-ledger filter, by the design's own explicit choice, §3.2), so the ONLY thing preventing a second send is sendLedgeredNotification's ledger insert colliding on the already-written (registrationId, 'no_show_reason_request') row -- a DB constraint that survives a process restart, unlike an in-memory guard. Also confirmed there is no second/reminder job anywhere in this file (grepped for a second ScheduledJobDefinition or a second NotificationKind member): the 'ask once, ever' guarantee rests structurally on there being exactly one job plus the ledger's UNIQUE constraint, matching REQ-031's identical mechanism. PASS.

S10 (transactional vs marketing distinguished; blocked users skipped in both) -- PASS. makeNoShowReasonRequestJob's call to sendLedgeredNotification (line 144-153) passes classification: 'transactional' explicitly, satisfying AC6/AC7's transactional requirement ('the message reaches a user with broadcast_opt_in=false') the same structural way REQ-025/031 already do. Re-read domain/notification.ts directly rather than trusting the design doc's description: the blocked-user check (`if (user.blocked) return { kind: 'skipped-blocked' }`, line 116) runs unconditionally, BEFORE the classification branch that reads broadcastOptIn (line 122, `if (input.classification === 'marketing' && !user.broadcastOptIn)`) -- this new call site cannot bypass the blocked-skip because it uses the exact same sendLedgeredNotification entry point every other kind uses; no parallel or bypassing send path was introduced anywhere in noShowJobs.ts (confirmed by grep: the only notification-sending call in the file is the one sendLedgeredNotification invocation). broadcastOptIn is read only inside the marketing-classification branch, which is structurally unreached for a 'transactional' kind -- so a no-show-reason-request reaches a broadcast_opt_in=false user, mirroring REQ-031's identical AC7-equivalent finding. PASS.

S1 (consent precedes storage) -- PASS. This flow only ever acts on a registration that already exists (a registration row is created at registration time, long before an event can finish and this job can select it) -- getRegistrationNoShowContext/selectRegistrationsForNoShowReasonRequest both read existing rows, never create a User or Registration. The reasoning mirrors REQ-031's own S1 finding verbatim: nobody without an existing consented User/Registration row (i.e. someone who already passed consent_pd_at at registration time) can ever reach this flow, since the selection query's own admission='admitted' clause presupposes a prior, already-consented registration. The free-text 'other' answer is not a new consent category under S1's own three-row table (store/message/publish) -- it is voluntarily authored content by an already-consented person in direct response to the bot's own prompt, the identical treatment REQ-031's feedback free-text fields (liked/improve) already received and were found not to need a fourth consent category. PASS.

S11 (no PII in plaintext logs) -- PASS. Grepped apps/bot/src for console./logger./log( across every new/changed file relevant to this diff (handlers/noShow.ts, scheduler/noShowJobs.ts, and the diff hunks in domain/registration.ts, domain/notification.ts): zero matches. The free-text no_show_reason content (the 'other' answer, potentially containing personal narrative) is never logged, echoed to any third party, or included in any AuditLog payload -- confirmed by grep that no writeAuditLog/AuditLog call exists anywhere in handlers/noShow.ts or scheduler/noShowJobs.ts (the only AuditLog call sites in domain/registration.ts, at lines 241/432/548/772/984/999/1312/1554, are all pre-existing functions this diff does not touch -- overrideAdmitAndCheckIn and similar admission-state-change functions, unrelated to writeNoShowReason). This is correct: S8 requires an AuditLog row only for a status change, and a no-show-reason answer is not a Registration/EventStaff/admission status change, so no AuditLog write should exist here, and none does -- meaning there is no AuditLog-payload leak vector for this free text either. PASS.

S13 (migration safety) -- explicitly confirmed, and unusual as flagged: `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/drizzle/` is EMPTY (re-ran directly as part of this review, output above under 'Bash: git diff master...HEAD --stat' confirms zero drizzle/ files in the changed-file list). There is no migration in this diff to review for drop/rename/rewrite safety -- DATA-DESIGNER's REQ-032-schema.md decision (reusing the existing unused registrations.no_show_reason text column added by REQ-011's migration 0001_tired_annihilus.sql, confirmed present and untouched) means REQ-032 needed zero schema change. Nothing in this diff drops, renames, or rewrites any column or table holding personal data or attendance history. No sign-off is owed under the migration-review duty because there is no migration; this N/A is stated explicitly per this role's own 'silent skip is a FAIL' rule, not silently assumed.

The 'no_show never stored as boolean' invariant (PRD 5 / PRD 13 AC8 / this requirement's own AC4) -- PASS, verified as if it were a numbered invariant. Grepped the entire diff (git diff master...HEAD) for `no_show` (non-reason), `noShow` as a column/field name distinct from `noShowReason`, and any boolean column pattern: the only persisted artifact anywhere in this diff is `registrations.no_show_reason` (pre-existing `text`, unchanged in schema.ts -- confirmed schema.ts does not even appear in `git diff master...HEAD --stat`'s file list, meaning it was not touched at all this requirement). `isNoShow` (domain/registration.ts lines 1409-1425) is a pure function taking evaluationTime as an explicit parameter (decisions/0006) and returning a boolean directly to its caller -- it is called exactly once, at send-composition time (scheduler/noShowJobs.ts line 115, inside composeNoShowReasonRequest), and its return value is used only in an `if` condition to decide whether to skip; it is never assigned to a variable that reaches a `.set(...)`/`.insert(...)` call, never cached, never written anywhere. No job or handler in this diff writes any boolean no-show value to any column. PASS.

Other invariants (S4-S8, S12, S14): N/A to this diff, with reason -- no qr_token/InviteCode generation or validation (S4), no check-in logic (S5), no checked_in_at write (S6 -- checkedInAt is read-only throughout this diff, part of the isNoShow input and the ownership-context read, never set), no capacity/admission-state changes (S7), no status-change AuditLog write is added or should be (S8, confirmed above under S11), no CSV export (S12), no Profile/speaker publication touched (S14). Confirmed by reading the full diff stat (16 files, none of them staff.ts/checkin handlers/exports/Profile-publication files) and each changed file directly rather than assuming from the requirement's own description.

invariant_verdicts.S1: PASS -- flow only acts on existing, already-consented Registration/User rows; free-text 'other' answer is not a 4th consent category, mirroring REQ-031's identical finding for its own free-text fields
invariant_verdicts.S2: PASS -- collapses to the S3 ownership check; no role/EventStaff dimension applies to a registrant answering their own question
invariant_verdicts.S3: PASS, re-verified hard as directed -- all three handlers (fixed-reason callback, 'other' callback, text-reply listener) resolve identity exclusively from the ACTING Telegram user's own tg_id via getFlowUserByTgId, never trust the registrationId in callback_data/ref-line as authorization; negative case constructed for each: a forged/leaked reference resolves to a mismatched context.userId !== flowUser.id and is refused with no write in all three paths
invariant_verdicts.S6: N/A -- checked_in_at is read-only throughout this diff, never set
invariant_verdicts.S8: N/A -- a no-show-reason answer is not a status change; correctly no AuditLog write added
invariant_verdicts.S9: PASS -- idempotency rests entirely on notification_ledger's UNIQUE(registration_id, kind) DB constraint plus the structural absence of any second/reminder job; no in-memory state; survives restarts
invariant_verdicts.S10: PASS -- classification: 'transactional' explicit on the one send site; sendLedgeredNotification's blocked-user skip runs unconditionally before the classification branch and is not bypassed by this new call site
invariant_verdicts.S11: PASS -- zero log/console/logger calls in any changed file; no AuditLog write exists (correctly) so no free-text no_show_reason content can leak via an audit payload either
invariant_verdicts.S13: N/A, explicitly confirmed rather than silently skipped -- git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/drizzle/ is empty; DATA-DESIGNER's decision reuses the existing REQ-011 column unchanged; no migration exists to sign off on
invariant_verdicts.no_show_never_boolean: PASS -- isNoShow is a pure function whose return value is used only in an if-condition to gate message composition; no job/handler writes a boolean no-show value to any column; schema.ts is not even touched by this diff
